title.narrative: Strengthening Comprehensive Primary Health Care in Urban Areas Program under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission

description.narrative: The proposed results-based lending will support the government in improving equitable access to comprehensive primary health care in urban areas. The government prioritizes the comprehensive primary health care as a strategy to achieve continuum of health care and resilient health systems to the COVID-19 pandemic and future health emergencies. The program outcome will be achieved through (i) expanding the number and range of primary health care services, especially noncommunicable diseases, infectious disease surveillance, and specialist services; (ii) strengthening community outreach services for easier access to health care services as well as improved health seeking behaviors among the urban poor and the vulnerable; and (iii) strengthening urban health system capacity for comprehensive, quality primary health care. The program aims to increase the number of functional health and wellness centers to cater 256 million urban dwellers including 51 million urban slum dwellers in 13 states. The program is aligned with the government's Ayushman Bharat (Healthy India) as well as Pradhan Mantri Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana (Epidemic / Disaster Preparedness and Response) programs.

description.narrative: Equitable access to quality comprehensive primary health care services in urban areas improved in 13 states

Number of cumulative screenings of cervical and breast cancer increased to at least 1.76 million (FY2020 baseline: 1.47 million) (PAP 2.3) Achievement: 7,708,878 Progress/Status: Cumulatively for the period of January 2022 to March 2025 the total screenings for cervical and breast cancer is 3,69,36,139
For the period Jan-March 2025, the total screenings were 1,41,87,727 Data Source: HWC Portal Actual value: 7,708,878

Annual utilization of urban HWCs increased to at least 20.98 million with at least 50% of visits made by women (FY2020 baseline: 17.48 million patient visits) (DLI 1) Achievement: 99883944 Progress/Status: Cumulatively for the period of January 2022 to March 2025 the total footfall is 28,07,04,699 and out of which footfall/visits made by women is 15,59,02,356 which is 55.54%.
For the period Jan 2025 - March 2025, the total footfall is 1,88,59,362 out of which footfall /visits made by women is 1,03,23,995 which is 55 % Data Source: HWC Portal

Annual number of screenings for diabetes and hypertension increased to at least 6.37 million (FY2020 baseline: 5.79 million) (DLI 2) Achievement: 45,752,145 Progress/Status: Cumulatively for the period of January 2022 to March 2025 the total screenings for Diabetes and Hypertension is 21,68,49,496
For the period Jan-March 2025, the total screenings is 7,61,13,611 Data Source: HWC Portal Actual value: 45,752,145

Urban pregnant women accessing at least 4 antenatal care check-ups in urban primary health facilities increased to 75% (FY2020 baseline: 72%) Achievement: 75 Progress/Status: Cumulatively for the period of January 2022 to March 2025 the total ANC registered 83,73,407 and 67,79,431 (80.96%) received over 4 ANC and above.
For the period Jan-March 2025, 6,87,678 registered and 5,82,699 (85%) received over 4 ANC and above Data Source: HMIS
